name: AI for Developers

hlido_opinion.headline: A clean, well-curated directory of AI developer tools — useful as a map of the category, but it is a listing site rather than an agent, and it offers no evidence behind the rankings it presents.
hlido_opinion.body: Taken as what it is, this is a tidy piece of work. The copy is honest about its purpose ('no fluff, just a curated list'), the entries are written by someone who has evidently used the tools — the Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, Copilot and Ollama descriptions are accurate and specific rather than scraped marketing lines — and the taxonomy (#ide, #coding-agents, #agent-harnesses, #inference-serving) is more useful than the usual alphabet soup. Filters for free, students and open source address real buyer constraints, and the submit-and-login flow suggests an intent to maintain it rather than publish once and leave. The problem is what it claims implicitly. 'Top pick' and 'Featured' badges sit beside Cursor and Claude Code with no stated criteria, no methodology, no test, and no disclosure of whether placement is paid, sponsored or affiliate-driven — and 'Sort by Popular' ranks without saying what popularity is measured from. A directory that ranks tools is making a recommendation, and a recommendation with no disclosed basis is an opinion wearing the clothes of a finding. There is no last-reviewed date on any entry, so a reader cannot tell whether a description reflects the tool today. There is also a category question this register should state plainly: this is a human-browsed listing site, not an AI agent, and it exposes no API, feed or machine-readable surface — so for the agent-to-agent use case that most of this corpus serves, it has essentially nothing to offer. It is a reasonable bookmark for a developer and not a tool an agent can use.

tier_rationale: FADING (57) because the curation is genuinely good and the descriptions are accurate, but the surface ranks and badges tools with no disclosed criteria and no affiliate or sponsorship disclosure, carries no last-reviewed dates, and offers no machine-readable surface at all. It is also, strictly, a directory rather than an agent. Published ranking criteria, a monetisation disclosure and dated entries would move it to STEADY.
what_it_does_well: Entry descriptions are accurate and specific — written by someone who has used the tools rather than pasted from vendor copy
A genuinely useful taxonomy (#ide, #coding-agents, #agent-harnesses, #inference-serving) instead of generic categories
Filters that match real buyer constraints: free, students, open source
Honest about its own scope — 'no fluff, just a curated list' is exactly what it delivers
A submit-and-login flow implies ongoing maintenance rather than a one-time publish
what_it_fails_at: 'Top pick' and 'Featured' badges are applied with no published criteria and no test behind them
No disclosure of whether placement or featuring is paid, sponsored or affiliate-driven
'Sort by Popular' ranks tools without stating what popularity is measured from
No last-reviewed date on any entry, so a reader cannot tell how current a description is
No API, feed or machine-readable surface — an agent cannot consume it
It is a directory, not an AI agent, so most of this register's evaluation axes do not apply to it
best_for: Developers orienting themselves in the AI tooling category who want an accurate, readable map
Students and open-source users who want to filter a long list down to what they can actually access
Anyone looking for a starting shortlist rather than a buying decision
not_recommended_for: Anyone treating 'Top pick' as an evidence-based recommendation — no criteria or testing is disclosed
Agents or programmatic consumers: there is no machine-readable surface
Buyers who need to know when an entry was last checked
Anyone who needs to know whether placements are paid
red_flags: The site ranks and badges products ('Top pick', 'Featured', 'Sort by Popular') with no published criteria and no affiliate, sponsorship or monetisation disclosure — a recommendation whose basis is unstated
No entry carries a last-reviewed date, so descriptions of a fast-moving category cannot be dated by the reader
Listed in this register under an agent category, but it is a human-browsed directory with no agent-facing surface at all

compared_to.verdict_diff: Genspark generates answer pages on demand from live sources; this is a hand-curated static directory. The directory is more trustworthy per entry and far narrower; Genspark is broader and less accountable per claim.

Perplexity answers a tooling question with citations you can follow; this directory gives you a browsable shortlist with no sources behind its rankings. Use Perplexity when you need the reasoning, the directory when you want a map.

evidence_urls.claim: A curated directory of AI agents, SDKs, coding copilots and developer tools
Entries are tagged by taxonomy (#ide, #coding-agents, #agent-harnesses, #inference-serving) and filterable by free / students / open source
Applies 'Top pick' and 'Featured' badges and offers 'Sort by Popular'
Accepts community submissions behind a login

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: None advertised. The captured surface is a human-browsed HTML directory with no API, feed, export or machine-readable manifest, so an agent has no documented way to query it.
